chunks: A shaykh from the people of hadith called Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan, known as Abu Ali b. Abd Rabbih al-'Adl, narrated this hadith to us. He said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Kufi al-Ju'fi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Abdullah al-Sijzi Abu Ishaq narrated to us from Yahya b. al-Husayn al-Mashhadi from Abu Harun al-Abdi from Rabi'a al-Sa'di.
He said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'By the star when it fades away.' He said: It is the star that fell at the break of dawn into the room of Ali b. Abi Talib.

My father al-Abbas wanted that star to fall in his house so he could possess the deputyship, vicegerency, and Imamate. However, God refused that for anyone other than Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and that is the favour of God which He gives to whomever He wills.

key_terms.الإمامة: The Imamate — the divinely ordained leadership in Shi'a theology
key_terms.الخلافة: The vicegerency/caliphate — political and spiritual leadership after the Prophet
key_terms.الوصية: The deputyship/succession — the appointment of Ali as the Prophet's successor
key_terms.فضل الله: The favour of God — God's sovereign grace in choosing whom He wills
key_terms.والنجم إذا هوى: By the star when it fades away — the opening verse of Surah al-Najm (53:1), interpreted here as referring to a celestial sign of divine designation

ai.seo_question: What is the Shi'a interpretation of 'By the star when it fades away' (Quran 53:1) according to Ibn Abbas?
ai.summary: This hadith offers a Shi'a exegesis of Quran 53:1 ('By the star when it fades away'). Rabi'a al-Sa'di asked Ibn Abbas about this verse, and he interpreted it as referring to a literal star that descended at dawn and fell into the dwelling of Ali b. Abi Talib, designating him as the Prophet's successor. Ibn Abbas candidly admits that his own father al-Abbas had hoped the star would fall into his home, granting him the succession, caliphate, and Imamate, but God decreed it exclusively for Ali.
